questions: Did s-bend progress rise above 0.15 at y = 0.08 m, or is it flat (the diminishing return expected from 0.05 to 0.07 m)?
Did steering_oscillation stay below 0.16 on all tracks? If it rose above 0.16 with line loss at zero, revert to y = 0.07 m.
Did line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom stay at one per run, or rise? If they rose, the sensors are seeing the bend too early, so return to y = 0.07 m.
Is max_error on the s-bend still near 0.066 m, and does any track get closer to completion?
Which track ends off track first, and at what progress? Does the slalom progress hold at about 0.107?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp that gave the best rms_error with this layout, and which sensors carry the most signal when the robot is on the line.

intent: Test the next forward sensor offset, y = 0.08 m (the contract maximum), on the iteration 6 platform. Hold the seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at ±0.048 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, radius 0.03 m and body 0.12 × 0.16 m. This isolates forward lead against iteration 6. Expect s-bend progress of about 0.15 to 0.16 (a small gain), steering_oscillation below 0.16, and the oval unchanged at zero line loss. If s-bend progress is flat or oscillation passes 0.16, revert to y = 0.07 m and treat forward lead as exhausted.
learning: Iteration 6 (y = 0.07 m) moved s-bend progress only from 0.1475 to 0.15, with line loss and max_error unchanged. Forward lead is near its plateau. Iteration 7 tests y = 0.08 m, the last point of the lead range. If that also plateaus, the remaining s-bend and slalom failures (max_error near 0.066 m with one line-loss event) are not fixed by geometry along the forward axis, and the next geometry test should be a drivetrain or body change rather than more lead.
rationale: Iteration 6 (y = 0.07 m) gave a score of 51.6166, up from 51.0692. The s-bend progress rose only from 0.1475 to 0.15, and max_error stayed at about 0.066 m, past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Steering oscillation was 0.1407, below the 0.16 trigger. Line loss stayed at one event per run on the s-bend and slalom, so it did not rise. The oval was unchanged (progress 0.115, zero line loss). Slalom progress was 0.1066, roughly flat. The Integrator's rule applies: s-bend progress rose, oscillation is below 0.16, and line loss did not rise, so keep the forward lead and test the next offset. The gain from 0.05 to 0.07 m was small (about 0.0025 progress), so the lead is near its plateau and I should expect less from 0.08 m. I still take the one-step test because it is cheap and the contract maximum is 0.08 m. Everything else stays fixed: seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 × 0.16 m, and kp, weights and line loss left to the Integrator. Hypothesis: s-bend progress will reach about 0.15 to 0.16 and line loss stays at one per run. If progress does not rise or oscillation exceeds 0.16, I will return to y = 0.07 m and treat forward lead as exhausted. The next lever would then be a drivetrain or body change, since the sensors are not the limit. Expected result at y = 0.08 m: s-bend progress 0.15 to 0.16, oscillation below 0.16, oval unchanged, and no completion on any track.
